key_insight: A shared, domain-pretrained model forecasts distributed PV generation across sites and horizons, enabling deployment at unseen stations without site-specific retraining.
engineering_relevance: Fleet-wide forecasting could reduce model training and maintenance while supporting adaptation to local operating needs as station data become available.
method: Formulate forecasting as sequence completion using historical PV power, weather observations, future NWP forecasts, and time encodings.
Pretrain across heterogeneous stations and forecast horizons with forecast-aligned, generic, or mixed reconstruction objectives.
Use mixed reconstruction to balance forecasting accuracy, robustness to degraded NWP, and downstream adaptation.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covers 479 PV stations—340 for development and 139 spatially held out for zero-shot testing—with reported gains over station-specific, shared, and generalist time-series baselines across 6-hour to 7-day horizons.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical error reductions, so the practical magnitude of gains and performance under local data conditions require verification.
paper_title: Foundation-Style Pretraining for Scalable and Transferable Distributed PV Forecasting
